adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent, the fallback branch runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but it then does `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, comparing each `cal.externalId` against a falsy `externalCalendarId` (undefined/null/"") and therefore typically never matching, yielding `selectedCalendar` undefined. The old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (now effectively the first element’s externalId), so this is a regression when references don’t carry `externalCalendarId` but `event.destinationCalendar` is populated. The diff shows multiple places now pass null/undefined externalCalendarId (e.g., EventManager builds `calenderExternalId` as null when missing), making this reachable and likely to break Google update calls that require `calendarId`.
